messages:
acme-ops: hey team, started seeing intermittent 429s and p95/p99 spikes from our dedicated eu-west-1 pool around 09:12 UTC. overall qps steady but tail latency jumps to ~3.6s; looks like this started after the autoscale tweak yesterday.
jess-support: thanks for flagging — can you share pool id + a sample request id? any recent model changes? :thinking:
acme-ops: pool id: rdw-ded-euw1-cc12, sample req: rq_0a3b2c. no model changes on our side. quick log snippet from our client:
```
{"req_id":"rq_0a3b2c","status":429,"msg":"rate limited by backend","latency_ms":3620,"route":"/v1/generate"}
```
we also saw a steady increase in internal retries around the same window.
mike-sre: @jess-support fyi this smells like noisy-cohost MIG interference — SM util and memory BW bursts can push p95 up without qps change. can you paste the node-level alert timeline? oncall-bot should have those metrics.
oncall-bot: ALERT node gpu01.euw3.slice2 — SM_util=96% (09:11-09:18 UTC), L3_bw_spike=high, MIG_slices_active=4, throttle_events=3
jess-support: got it. @mike-sre @taylor-eng can we triage whether this is kernel-level contention (SM/mem) vs scheduling hold? customer is on fractional MIG packing config.
taylor-eng: quick triage plan: 1) repro with synthetic load pinned to that pool, 2) collect per-slice sm_util, l3_bw, mem_bw, 3) try pinning tenant to an isolated slice to see delta. temporary mitigation: reduce concurrency or enable fallback to smaller model variant.
mike-sre: repro command (low-noise load):
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-small","prompt":"test","max_tokens":64}' &
done
```
watch node metrics: `rdw-cli node metrics gpu01.euw3 --slice 2 --metrics sm_util,l3_bw,mem_bw`
acme-ops: running the script now, will paste numbers in a minute. curious — if this is noisy neighbor, what's the short-term fix? our product team can't tolerate p99 > 2s.
jess-support: short-term: we can temporarily route your traffic to a compatible reserved slice (no billing change for short-term autoscale bump). longer-term: we recommend isolation (dedicated slice) or adjusting packing policy.
acme-ops: ran the repro — before pin: p95=3600ms p99=5400ms, sm_util bursts to 98%. after pinning to an isolated slice (support action) p95 dropped to 180ms p99=260ms. huge difference.
mike-sre: checks out. this confirms noisy neighbor on shared node — likely SM scheduling thrash causing long tail. next steps: (a) collect kernel traces for the busy slice, (b) evaluate autoscale policy to prefer isolation when tail > x, (c) consider adding placement rule to avoid mixed heavy batch tenants on same host.
taylor-eng: I'll open a follow-up internal ticket with traces + suggested scheduler tweak. tagging: @jess-support to coordinate communication with ACME and @infra-leads for slice placement change.
jess-support: noted — i will file incident INC-2026-324 and update ACME timeline. ACME, we'll keep you on the isolated slice while we investigate further. apologies for the disruption :pray:
acme-ops: appreciate the fast triage — keeping isolated slice for now. please let us know if you need any more logs from our side. :thumbsup:
jess-support: closing the support loop here: temporary mitigation applied, ticket created, eng investigating root cause (kernel/policy). we'll follow up with postmortem and billing note if any permanent capacity changes are needed.
